summary: Titanium oxide thin films were synthesized on the (0001) a-Al2O3 surface using molecular layering (ALD). The process involved chemisorption of TiCl4 followed by hydrolysis with water vapors. The film thickness increased by 0.25 nm per cycle after the first cycle, where an initial thickness of 0.75 nm was formed. The growth mechanism was identified as an intermediate case between layer-by-layer and island growth, closer to the Volmer-Weber model.
evidence: The synthesis of titanium oxide thin film was performed according to the following stages: 1. Preliminary heating of the substrate (a-Al2O3) in an atmosphere of air at 500°C; 2. Cooling of the substrate to 200°C in a dry helium flow; 3. Chemisorption of TiCl4 on the surface of the substrate at 200°C in a dry helium flow; 4. Removal of TiCl4 and HCI excess from the reactor by a helium flow at 200°C; 5. Hydrolysis of TiCl4 fixed on the surface of the substrate with water vapors in the nitrogen flow between 200 and 400°C. The film thickness increased by 0.25 nm per cycle after the first cycle, where an initial thickness of 0.75 nm was formed. The growth mechanism was identified as an intermediate case between layer-by-layer and island growth, closer to the Volmer-Weber model.
